page: Amazon Web Services m8gb.4xlarge is a general-purpose server instance powered by the ARM64 architecture. It features an AWS Graviton processor built on the ARMv9 Neoverse-V2 architecture, delivering 16 dedicated physical cores and 16 vCPUs operating at a clock speed of 2.8 GHz. The processor includes 64 KB of L1d cache, 2 MB of L2 cache, and 36 MB of L3 cache. The instance is equipped with 64.0 GB of system memory, providing a balanced allocation of 4.0 GB per core. It operates on the AWS Nitro hypervisor and provides a baseline network bandwidth of 33 Gbps. This instance does not include local storage or dedicated GPU hardware.

Benchmark data indicates strong memory subsystem performance, with the Passmark memory score ranking in the top tier. Large-block memory bandwidth is also strong, reaching 296.88 GB/sec for read-only and 138.33 GB/sec for write operations. Multi-threaded bzip3 decompression and Geekbench single-core and multi-core metrics also place in the top 25 percent. However, the instance exhibits average performance in standard CPU tasks, such as stress-ng multi-core execution, static web serving, and Redis SET operations.

Tradeoffs of the m8gb.4xlarge include the absence of local NVMe storage, requiring reliance on network-attached storage options. Additionally, the ARM64 architecture lacks x86-specific instruction sets like AVX or AMX. Performance is weak in specific LLM inference tasks, particularly text generation for small models and prompt processing for medium models. Given its balanced resource profile and strong memory bandwidth, this instance is well-suited for database operations, software compilation, general-purpose web serving, and multi-threaded data decompression tasks.
